notes.interpretation: Training caused complete model destabilization. The trained agent produces gibberish — token soup of code fragments, random Spanish, broken HTML, hash-IDs. The composite reward's 0.15 score is essentially the keyword 'refund' appearing somewhere in the soup. This is NOT subtle rubric overfitting; the model has drifted off the manifold of coherent English. Classic textbook RL-without-KL-anchor failure mode (see whitepaper §10.5 'Reference-model drift' and §11.5 failure-modes table). Default GSPOConfig has beta=0.0 and use_reference_model=False, so nothing pulls the policy back toward the SFT base. With a discrete-cliff keyword reward, tight clip, and 3 epochs on 16 examples, the model converged to 'any tokens containing keyword X' over 'coherent English containing keyword X'.

remaining_hypotheses_pre_demo: GSPO clip range overshoots on discrete-cliff keyword rewards
notes.diagnosis_post_demo: Falsifies all three. None of them produce gibberish output — they produce a *different but still-coherent* policy that happens to score worse on the rubric. The actual failure is unconstrained policy drift: no KL anchor (beta=0, use_reference_model=False) lets the policy walk to any local optimum on the reward surface, including 'produce keyword tokens with no other constraint on output coherence'.
notes.single_variable_fix_to_try: Set use_reference_model=True and beta=0.05 in GSPOConfig. This is the cheapest correction and the one most directly supported by §10.5 of the whitepaper. Expected outcome: trained model stays in the neighborhood of the SFT base and improvement (if any) is positive instead of catastrophic.
notes.framework_evidence: This is the first run in the session where the policy actually moved. Gradient path (GSPO clipped surrogate -> LoRA backward) is functional. The default GSPOConfig surface (beta=0.0, use_reference_model=False) is unsafe for small-corpus runs without an external KL anchor — this should be a flagged default in §B.1 of the whitepaper.
notes.v1_publication_gates: FAIL — improvement is negative AND trained model produces incoherent output. Cannot be cited as evidence of framework efficacy in any form.
